# Vela Design System

> A design system for data-heavy products, built first for security consoles. Two-layer colour architecture (primitives -> semantics), three
> deliberately separate status taxonomies, full light and dark theming, zero runtime dependencies
> in the core entry (the `/headless` entry needs one optional peer, Base UI, and is where Checkbox,
> Radio Group, Popover, Tooltip, Icon Button, Dialog, Toast and Dropdown List ship from).
> 80 of the 260 design rules are enforced by the TypeScript types; the rest are checked at runtime, in a
> real browser, or by review. Each rule in the component and contract guidelines is tagged with its level.
>
> THESE SPECS ARE FRAMEWORK-AGNOSTIC. The published package is a React implementation of them, and
> the code samples below are React — but the tokens, the closed prop sets, the taxonomies and the
> accessibility rules hold for any implementation. If you are generating for Angular, Vue or
> Svelte, follow every rule here and translate the syntax. Where a component documents a **pointer
> enhancement**, it is additive by definition: the component is complete, correct and accessible
> without it, every rule here still holds, and skipping it costs feel and never function. An
> enhancement may not change the props, the markup contract or what the CSS does on its own — if
> yours would, it is not an enhancement. Never invent one. For Flutter, the same tokens ship as
> `tokens.dart` (`VelaColors`, `VelaSizing`, `VelaTypography`, `velaThemeData`) — bind `VelaColors`
> semantics, never `VelaPrimitives`.

Read **`DESIGN.md`** first. It ships at the package root (`node_modules/@omkarux/vela/DESIGN.md`,
`../DESIGN.md` from this file) and sits at the repository root. It is the single global-rules
document: the token grammar, the three taxonomies, closed prop sets, states, motion, theming,
responsive and density rules, what CI asserts for accessibility, every anti-pattern, and what is not in the kit. Then
`overview.md`, which maps a user need to a component and lists the choices agents most often get
wrong. Then the per-component file before generating any markup.

`proposals/` (in the repository, not the npm package) holds specs for components that are NOT
built yet — Verdict Card, Action Impact Card, Autonomy Ladder, Approval Queue, Calibrated Confidence Gate, Evidence Locker, Agent Provenance Badge, Awareness Clock, Override & Teach Panel. Never import or imitate them; name
the closest component that exists and flag the gap.

Working from the Figma library? `figma-map.json` (this folder) maps each component set to the
export and props to write for it. When a design node is an instance of a Vela set, write that
export; never reproduce the markup Figma's design context generates for it.

Looking for a component by machine? `components.json` (this folder) lists every built component:
its purpose, status, where to import it from, its "When to use" text, its props with their closed
values, defaults and which are required, and its tokens. It is generated from the specs on every
build; each spec stays the full contract.

Working in a coding agent? The Vela skill (`skills/vela/SKILL.md` in the repository) sends an agent
through these files in order and ends the run with the report below. Install it in a project with
`npx skills add omkarpkh/vela`.

## Hard rules (apply everywhere)
- Bind SEMANTIC tokens (`var(--vela-text-default)`). Never a primitive (`--vela-grey-700`), never raw hex.
- Numeric tokens already carry their unit. Use `var(--vela-space-10)`, never `calc(var(--vela-space-10) * 1px)`.
- Prop sets are CLOSED. If a value is not in the component's Props table, it does not exist.
- Never invent a component. If nothing fits, say so and name the closest match.
- Severity, Risk and Status are three different taxonomies. Never cross them.
- Icons come from `ICON_NAMES` only (`<Icon name="…" />`). Never import `lucide-react` or another icon set beside Vela.

## When you finish: the report

Every run that builds with Vela (a page, a pattern, a demo) ends with a report of what it used,
what it made itself and the gaps it found. It is a list for a reviewer. There is no percentage and
no score. Four groups, always in this order, as headings. Write "None." under a group that is empty.

Before a component goes under Used, check the job you gave it against its "When to use" lines
(that section of its spec, or `whenToUse` in `components.json`). Each line routes a need to a
component, and many say where a need goes instead: a Risk Pill's lines send "an event the user
must read" to a Contextual Alert. A component doing a job its lines send elsewhere is a misuse:
fix it, and do not list it as Used. A need whose line says "not in this kit" is a Flagged gap.

1. **Used.** Each Vela export you rendered, with the props you set, and its import path:
   `Button variant="primary"` from `@omkarux/vela`.
2. **Built from tokens.** Your own layout and glue that binds only semantic tokens: a page grid, a
   summary row, the gap between two sections. Name the tokens. This is ordinary work, not invention.
3. **Invented.** Anything else: a component from another library, a component you wrote that looks
   or acts like a control, any raw colour, any primitive token, any raw length. One line each on
   why nothing in Vela fit.
4. **Flagged gaps.** A need Vela does not cover, one entry each:
   - **Need:** the task, not the widget ("choosing which analyst an alert goes to", not "a select").
   - **Closest:** the nearest component, by its `name` in `components.json`.
   - **Why not:** the rule in its spec that rules it out, quoted, with the spec and section.
   - **File it:** a link that opens the component-request form with the need, the closest and the
     reason already written in.

The link opens `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/component-request.yml` by its field ids. Encode every value
with `encodeURIComponent` (a space is `%20`, a newline `%0A`, `"` is `%22`, `&` is `%26`, `#` is
`%23`, `[` and `]` are `%5B` and `%5D`):

```
https://github.com/omkarpkh/vela/issues/new?template=component-request.yml
  &title=<%5BComponent%5D the need, short, (closest: name)>
  &need=<the need>
  &gap=<Closest: name. Then the quoted rule>
```

(one line, no spaces; broken here to read). The link fills the form's text fields: `title`, `need`
and `gap`. It cannot fill the "Closest existing component" menu, which is a dropdown (tested
signed in, 7 November 2026: the menu opened on its default). So the link has no `closest`, the
closest component goes in the title and at the start of `gap`, and whoever files the issue picks it
in the menu. A link longer than GitHub accepts fails (414), so quote the rule, not the whole
section.

A short report, for an alerts triage page:

```
## Vela report

### Used
- `Table caption="Open alerts" density="compact"`, with `Table.Head`, `Table.Body`, `Table.Row`, `Table.HeaderCell`, `Table.Cell`, from `@omkarux/vela`
- `RiskPill risk="high"` from `@omkarux/vela`
- `StatusIndicator status="unhealthy" label="Agent offline"` from `@omkarux/vela`
- `Button variant="primary"` ("Assign") from `@omkarux/vela`

### Built from tokens
- The page grid: two columns, `gap: var(--vela-space-20)`, on `var(--vela-bg-global)`.
- The summary row: counts in `var(--vela-text-heading)`, labels in `var(--vela-text-de-emphasized)`, `gap: var(--vela-space-10)`.

### Invented
- A native `<select>` for the assignee. Nothing in Vela is a form select; see the gap below.

### Flagged gaps
- Need: choosing which analyst an alert is assigned to, in a form that is saved later.
  Closest: Dropdown List.
  Why not: "A Dropdown List has no "nothing chosen" and is never inside a form." (dropdown-list.md, When to use)
  File it: https://github.com/omkarpkh/vela/issues/new?template=component-request.yml&title=%5BComponent%5D%20Pick%20an%20assignee%20in%20a%20form%20(closest%3A%20Dropdown%20List)&need=Choosing%20which%20analyst%20an%20alert%20is%20assigned%20to%2C%20in%20a%20form%20that%20is%20saved%20later.&gap=Closest%3A%20Dropdown%20List.%0A%0A%3E%20A%20Dropdown%20List%20has%20no%20%22nothing%20chosen%22%20and%20is%20never%20inside%20a%20form.%20(dropdown-list.md%2C%20When%20to%20use)
```

## Figma

A matching Figma library exists: **Vela Design System**
(https://www.figma.com/design/XO2rmeCcgOjyKe4oipgF4j/Vela-Design-System). It is *compiled from this contract*, not
the source of it — 237 variables and 6 component sets mirroring the token architecture 1:1, with
every variable carrying its `var(--vela-*)` name for Dev Mode. Each component's per-file
`## Figma mapping` section states which Figma property corresponds to which prop, and which
behaviour has no Figma expression at all.

## Components
- [Button](components/button.md)
- [Toggle](components/toggle.md)
- [Input](components/input.md)
- [Text Area](components/text-area.md) — `@omkarux/vela`, Experimental
- [Contextual Alert](components/contextual-alert.md)
- [Status Indicator](components/status-indicator.md)
- [Risk Pill](components/risk-pill.md)
- [Tabs](components/tabs.md) — when the row is full both entries fade the edge where more tabs are and scroll a tab you open, click or focus wholly into view; the headless Tabs also puts the tabs that don't fit into "N more" (a Dropdown List of every tab) and keeps the open tab in view. The count is measured, never a prop; `unseen` (headless `Tabs.Trigger` only) adds "· 1 new"
- [Icon](components/icon.md) — 50 curated Lucide glyphs (ISC, see NOTICE), compiled into the core entry; `ICON_NAMES` is the closed list; Experimental
- [Brand Mark](components/brand-mark.md) — `@omkarux/vela`, Experimental: GitHub's and Figma's own marks, unmodified (see NOTICE), only to link to their services; `name` is `github` or `figma`, nothing else; no Figma set yet
- [Checkbox](components/checkbox.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental
- [Radio Group](components/radio-group.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental
- [Table](components/table.md) — `@omkarux/vela`, Experimental
- [Popover](components/popover.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental
- [Tooltip](components/tooltip.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental (`kind="label"` repeats a control's name and is heard once; `TooltipProvider` groups a row, so the next opens at once)
- [Icon Button](components/icon-button.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental: one glyph (`icon`, `brandMark` or `word="npm"`), always named by `label`, a button (`onClick`) or a link (`href`), 24 or 35px; no Figma set yet
- [Dialog](components/dialog.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental (with `variant="alert"`)
- [Toast](components/toast.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental (`ToastProvider` + `useToast()`)
- [Dropdown List](components/dropdown-list.md) — `@omkarux/vela/headless` only, Experimental (Base UI `Menu`; Figma set published 31 Oct 2026)

## Contracts
A contract has rules and no UI: plain functions every surface shares.
- [Filter Grammar](contracts/filter-grammar.md) — `@omkarux/vela`, Experimental: `defineFields` declares a host's fields once (type and trust); every filter, typed, linked, saved or emitted by an agent, is checked against it, with one text form and one readback sentence. Never invent a filter syntax.
